chapters.title: Module 1 – Using language to provide personal information

lessons.title: Situation 1: Undergoing a job interview (revision of problem areas)
Situation 2: Applying for a passport (tense review; present perfect and future continuous)
Situation 3: Discussing recreational activities (question tags)
Situation 4: Anticipating one's second-language needs at work (phrasal verbs and prepositional phrases)

chapters.title: Module 2 – Using language to talk about consumer economy, community resources and time management

lessons.title: Situation 1: Comparing prices or quality to find the best buys (adverbs for, since, ago)
Situation 2: Using banking services (complex sentences)
Situation 3: Helping with fund-raising and support groups for community resources (expressing preferences)
Situation 4: Taking part and managing time in community, workplace and school activities (other forms of comparison)

chapters.title: Module 3 – Using language to talk about health care and environmental awareness

lessons.title: Situation 1: Health problems related to drugs, tobacco, alcohol abuse and ageing (relative clauses)
Situation 2: Preventing communicable diseases in schools, workshops and the community (direct and indirect speech)
Situation 3: Environmental issues such as climate change and global warming (first, second and third conditionals)
Situation 4: Garbage collection, disposal and recycling services (structures with adjectives)

chapters.title: Module 4 – Using language to talk about rights and civic responsibilities

lessons.title: Situation 1: Volunteering in gender equality promotion activities (direct and indirect speech, revision)
Situation 2: Participating in training activities and courses on democracy (phrasal verbs)
Situation 3: Taking part in polls and surveys (sequence of tenses; word order)
Situation 4: Campaigning and voting for leaders (phrasal verbs in expressions of purpose)

chapters.title: Module 5 – Using language to explore and keep abreast with audio-visual and print media and ICTs

lessons.title: Situation 1: Subscribing to service packages (telephone and internet services)
Situation 2: Using ICTs to enhance work or learning
Situation 3: Using ICTs as recreational resources at home or in the community (active and passive voices)
Situation 4: Facing difficulties with the use of ICTs at work or for learning
